metadata.case_name: SUSI YANTI & ANOTHER v. CHU SHIU-CHUEN

injuries.description: Multiple abrasions and laceration wounds with puncture wounds over both upper and lower limbs resulting in extensive permanent scarring
injuries.body_part: both upper and lower limbs (including right leg, left calf, upper right arm)
source: Upon admission to the Yan Chai Hospital on the day of the incident, the 1st plaintiff was found to have sustained multiple abrasions and laceration wounds over both upper and lower limbs.

Colour photographs taken at the time show quite serious scratch marks and puncture wounds on her limbs. More recent photographs demonstrate the existence of extensive, quite ugly scars. These scars are permanent and the plaintiff will have to live with them as best she can.

On 7 June 1999, she consulted Dr Ian Nicholson, a plastic surgeon, who made the following observations. There were no fewer than 19 very conspicuous, darkly pigmented, raised and scattered scars of significant dimensions on the back of the 1st plaintiff's right leg. There were also multiple faint abrasions and puncture scars on that limb. On her left calf, there were 4 obvious similar unsightly scars, as well as a number of faint, scattered abrasions and puncture markings.
2 noticeable raised, thickened and pigmented scars were discerned on her upper right arm, as well as faint abrasions.

injuries.description: Psychiatric injury: post-traumatic stress disorder, phobia of dogs and inferiority complex resulting in psychiatric disability
source: Dr Peter Ho Pang-nin, a psychiatrist, examined the 1st plaintiff on 13 August 2000. He noted that following the attack the 1st plaintiff has become tense and worried and suffered from time to time from depressive mood.
She confirmed in the witness-box that these nightmares have become less frequent, although her phobia of dogs which developed as a result of the attack has not lessened with time.

Dr Peter Ho also noted that the 1st plaintiff was embarrassed by the presence of the scars and has developed an inferiority complex as a result. He diagnosed that she has developed a phobia towards dogs and was suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder and inferiority complex as a result of what had befallen her.

injuries.description: Laceration wounds, bite and scratch marks to thighs and left arm resulting in permanent cosmetic scarring
injuries.body_part: thighs and left arm (including left shoulder, right thigh near knee, front of left upper thigh, back of upper thigh)
source: Upon admission to Yan Chai Hospital after the attack, this young victim was found to have 3 laceration wounds over both thighs and multiple minor bite and scratch marks over her thighs and left arm.

Dr Nicholson examined her on 7 June 1999 and noted that there was a faint pale scar over her left shoulder, a slightly noticeable pale scar on her right thigh near the knee region, a raised pale scar on the front of the left upper thigh as well as several barely perceptible bite marks and a slightly pigmented raised irregular laceration scar with 2 noticeable pairs of stitch marks on the back of her upper thigh. Dr Nicholson opined that these scars would become less significant in time but that this young patient has nonetheless sustained permanent cosmetic disability of the order of 1/4%.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple open wounds of hip or thigh

injuries.description: Psychiatric injury: phobia of dogs, apprehension and anxiety resulting in psychiatric impairment
source: Dr Peter Ho was consulted on 13 August 2000. His examination of the 2nd plaintiff confirmed that she had become apprehensive and tense, and fearful of dogs following her attack.
He commented that her phobia towards dogs would lead to anxiety whenever she encounters such animals. This psychiatric disability has resulted in impairment of the whole person of 2%.

manifestations.description: embarrassment by scars and inferiority complex
apprehension, tension and anxiety when encountering dogs

treatments_received: follow-up treatment at the Orthopaedics Ward of Yan Chai Hospital
treatments_future: psychiatric counselling and treatment for the 1st plaintiff (advised; judge allowed $72,000 for a 2 year course at about $3,000 per month)
psychiatric counselling for the 2nd plaintiff (advised for 1 year; judge awarded $24,000)

losses.description: Embarrassed by the presence of the scars and has developed an inferiority complex; avoids wearing shorts and skirts to conceal her disability.
Would be unable to take on employment in domestic households where dogs are kept (phobia of dogs impacting employment options).
Scarring that as she grows older would present a degree of embarrassment to her.
